heroHeadline: US Strikes IRGC Near Bandar Abbas — Iran Calls It 'Flagrant Ceasefire Violation'; IRGC Claims MQ-9 Downed; Israel Kills 31 in Lebanon, Deepens Ground Op; 4th Round Doha June 2–3; Day 89
heroSubtitle: Days 88–89 (May 26–27): A sharp military escalation threatened the peace track on Day 88 when US CENTCOM struck IRGC missile sites and mine-laying boats near Bandar Abbas — killing 4 IRGC navy officers. Iran called the strikes 'flagrant ceasefire violations,' noting its diplomatic delegation was mid-flight to Qatar when they occurred. The IRGC claimed it downed a US MQ-9 Reaper drone and fired on an F-35 over the Persian Gulf — the most direct Iranian kinetic actions of the post-ceasefire period. Iran's internet was partially restored on Day 88 after 88 days (2,093 hours) — the longest nationwide blackout in modern history. Despite the military incidents, a fourth round of direct US-Iran talks was scheduled for June 2–3 in Doha. On Day 89, Israeli strikes killed 31 in Lebanon — the deadliest single day in weeks — as Netanyahu declared Israel 'deepening' its operation and expanding ground forces beyond the Yellow Line into southern Lebanon and the Bekaa Valley. Trump said both sides were 'close to finalizing' a deal with 'strong inspections,' but Araghchi said he was 'unsure' of any imminent agreement, and Shamkhani again called US nuclear control demands a 'fantasy.'
